Ransomware Attack Disrupts Ghana’s Electric Utilities Sector

A major cyber attack has struck Ghana’s electric utilities industry, affecting the operations of Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd and other firms, as a ransomware campaign targets their information technology systems. The incident, which began late Monday, has led to significant disruptions in customer service, billing operations, and internal communications, with utility executives warning that restoration efforts are ongoing and the situation remains fluid.

According to sources within the industry, attackers gained access to corporate IT networks, encrypting files and demanding payment in cryptocurrency to restore access. As a result, customer service lines at affected utilities have been overwhelmed, with many callers reporting difficulties in accessing account information or paying bills online. Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd confirmed in a statement that its payment portal and customer management systems are currently offline, and that teams are “working around the clock” to restore operations.

Kwame Mensah, spokesperson for the Ghana Power Workers’ Union, told trade press, “Staff are doing their utmost to maintain field operations, but the IT outage is hampering coordination and delaying routine maintenance tasks. Our first priority is to ensure the continued supply of electricity, but these attacks are making it much harder to respond quickly to customer needs.”

Industry analysts warn that the attack exposes the vulnerability of the sector’s digitally connected infrastructure. “Ghana’s electric utilities have made significant investments in IT systems to modernize their networks, but this incident shows the risks that come with increased digitalization,” said energy sector analyst Akosua Boateng. She added, “With critical customer data and billing systems affected, companies may face revenue delays and reputational damage.”

The Ghana Utilities Association has called for urgent action to bolster cyber defenses across the industry. “This is a wake-up call. The sector must invest further in cybersecurity training, infrastructure upgrades, and contingency planning to prevent future incidents,” said the Association in a statement.

At the time of writing, electricity supply has not been widely disrupted, but companies have warned customers to expect delays in resolving account issues and service requests. Investigations are ongoing, and affected utilities have not indicated when normal operations will resume.
